title: Nonconvex-concave problems: arbitrary deterministic algorithms and game stationarity

task.objective: min_{x in X} Phi(x), Phi(x)=max_{y in Y}f(x,y)+indicator_X(x)

assumptions.scope: The complete stated domain. Constants remain uniform when the other variable block is fixed.
assumptions.description: The set $X$ is known, nonempty, closed, and convex. The set $Y$ is known, nonempty, compact, and convex, with $\operatorname{diam}(Y)\le D_y$.

assumptions.scope: The complete stated domain. Constants remain uniform when the other variable block is fixed.
assumptions.description: The function $f$ is jointly $\beta$-smooth on $X\times Y$. For every $x$, $f(x,\cdot)$ is concave. Convexity in the $x$ direction and a positive strong-concavity modulus are not required.

model.parameter_domain_description: $D_y$: nonnegative real; $\Delta$: positive real; $\beta$: positive real; $d$: integer at least 2; $\varepsilon$: positive real. Derived quantities are defined in the parameter table. Each region states any additional accuracy and dimension conditions.

objects.definition: The unknown real payoff is $f:X\times Y\to\mathbb R$, with primal variable $x\in X\subset\mathbb R^{d_x}$ and dual variable $y\in Y\subset\mathbb R^{d_y}$.
The feasible set is explicitly public. Exact projections and linear algebra use known geometry and reveal no hidden-function information.

norms.definition: The Euclidean norm and inner product are $\|v\|_2=(\sum_jv_j^2)^{1/2}$ and $\langle u,v\rangle=\sum_j u_jv_j$. On the joint space use $\|(x,y)\|_2=(\|x\|_2^2+\|y\|_2^2)^{1/2}$.
